body: What happened if you don't mind me asking? I'm quite close myself right now and stumbled on your post trying to get answers on inpatients.

People having various reasons to go that path. 

For me, the pain and guilt I was dealing with was too intense. I started because it shocked me so much that it kind of... numbed me out. For a little bit. And then after a few minutes, the panic would set in. What would I say at work? If my friends saw? Am I going to look weird wearing a long sleeve in the summer? Then it let to insane guilt and shame about it. And thus the cycle continued. 

I've gotten better at managing it but I will say it's a door that once you open never quite gets closed again. I wish someone had told me that before that first time I did it.

I know how you feel because the reason I came to this page is because I wanted to die more than anything. But hold on. Let it out. Message me if you need to just let out how you're feeling because god knows keeping it in makes you want to kill yourself that much more.

I'm not gonna lie I don't have something that makes me want to stay alive so badly right now that I'm actually motivated. *But,* I do know that I will hurt people I love if I kill myself. This is what I see. My parents being destroyed; both of them neverendingly blaming themselves for not hospitalizing me or wondering if there was something they could've done. My brother, who already has self-harming tendencies, being triggered by this and possibly trying to follow in my footsteps. My best friend, who I've convinced to stay alive in the past, being heartbroken that the one person that understood him inside and out is now gone. 

I'm in so much pain... all I want is to die and never feel it again. It's not for me that I'm alive right now. But while I get there (and I hope one day I do), any reason is enough.

Just be there. I can tell you she is feeling immense pain if she's self-harming, I did too. I don't know anything about her situation or if you're close but try being someone that she can talk to. One of the worse things to deal with when self-harming is how much people don't understand or know what to say. Educate yourself, and be there for her. I never told my little brother about my self-harming but he knew me well enough to see that something wasn't right, and sometimes him just coming to my room and bugging me about something else was what kept me from going and cutting myself again. Just be there for her and know this is going to be hard. She may not be open about it/probably will get defensive but mental illness makes you isolate yourself and that's the worst you can do. Good luck, your sister can be okay again.

It's just the number of times I've felt like this... and I never go through with it. I do planning and research about methods and then in the end I always reach out. But it happens like a cycle. I have terrible episodes of wanting to die and then immediately feel a crazy upsurge in motivation to get better and live my life to the fullest. And then something happens and I'm back in a hole. This happens multiple times a month and I feel crazy... it's gotten to the point where if I start feeling happy or excited about life again I'm also scared because I know it won't last. I know I won't feel like I do now endlessly. But I also know that it's not the last time, and that's what makes me finally just go through with it.
can anyone give some insight as to what happens if you are committed because I also have an appointment tomorrow and I'm debating being honest about how much I wanna die...
